posts.title: AI is dominating the conversation at Climate Week
posts.summary: This week, world leaders descended on Manhattan for the UN General Assembly. It’s also New York Climate Week—investors, policymakers, advocates, and journalists are colliding at panels, talks, and fancy dinners. With so many climate voices in one place, the discourse can feel a little louder than usual. This year, the unavoidable topic is artificial intelligence.…
bullets: Artificial intelligence has become the central theme at New York Climate Week, highlighting a growing tension between its potential for climate research and its massive energy consumption.
Big Tech firms are increasingly driving capital into energy startups, specifically in nuclear, geothermal, wind, and solar, to secure the power required for AI infrastructure.
The surge in AI-related electricity demand is forcing a rapid buildout of energy supplies, including emissions-heavy natural gas, which complicates global efforts to meet climate targets.

With the 1.5 °C warming threshold becoming increasingly difficult to maintain, the debate is shifting toward whether AI can effectively accelerate carbon removal technologies or if it will exacerbate the climate crisis.

posts.title: The Download: a bid to scrap the virtual wall and AI hits Climate Week
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. A congressional representative just proposed killing America’s border tower program Delia Ramirez, a Democratic US representative from Illinois, has announced plans to introduce legislation to terminate the surveillance tower program along…
bullets: US Representative Delia Ramirez has introduced legislation to terminate the billion-dollar 'virtual wall' surveillance tower program along the southern border.
An MIT Technology Review investigation found that nearly 1,100 people died within the range of these surveillance towers between 2015 and 2026, suggesting the system fails to prevent fatalities.
The report highlights a significant discrepancy between the program's multi-billion dollar cost and its operational effectiveness in detecting border crossings.
OpenAI's technology has reportedly executed the first known AI-driven hack of a government site, marking a new milestone in cybersecurity risks.

bullets: Transporting the native packetized traffic of the NoC directly across die boundaries using a stable, invariant interface.
The semiconductor industry is rapidly transitioning from monolithic SoCs to chiplet-based architectures.
At the same time, AI workloads are evolving beyond cloud inference into physical AI: systems that perceive, reason, and act in the real world.
Autonomous vehicles, industrial robots, humanoid robots, drones, and intelligent manufacturing systems all require continuous, high-volume data flow between heterogeneous compute engines.
However, these two trends expose a weakness in today’s die-to-die communication architectures.

posts.title: 3D Chips Push EDA Into New Territory
posts.summary:
As AI chips move to stacked, chiplet-based architectures, EDA vendors are reworking mature tools for cross-domain analysis, faster exploration, and agentic AI assistance. 
The post 3D Chips Push EDA Into New Territory appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: As AI chips move to stacked, chiplet-based architectures, EDA vendors are reworking mature tools for cross-domain analysis, faster exploration, and agentic AI assistance.

Key Takeaways:
As demand for AI power and performance grows, chip designs increasingly involve 3D stacking, chiplets, and heterogeneous integration within a single package.
In a virtuous cycle, EDA tool vendors are leveraging advanced chips to simulate multi-physics challenges in a single tool instead of running individual solvers.
Agentic AI is adding another layer of analysis to enable faster design exploration and automate various tasks.
However, a few speed bumps remain due to the rapid progression of chip technology.
